hook_text: 1,85 km shared by 4 runners. The trick? Add zeros.
clip_script: The relay team runs 1,85 km shared equally by four runners. Four into one does not go: write zero, and place the comma above the comma. Four into eighteen tenths goes four times, remainder two. Bring down five: twenty-five hundredths. Four goes six times, remainder one. The division has not finished, so add a zero and bring it down: ten thousandths. Four goes twice, remainder two. Add another zero: twenty. Four goes five times exactly. Answer: 0,4625 km per runner, which is 462,5 metres.
visual_style: A running track split into four relay legs; a long-division bracket fills in with the comma pinned above the comma and zeros sliding in at the end.
pacing: Fast steps, pause each time a zero slides in, finish on 462,5 m.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to handle remainders and recurring decimals.
